patients.summary: Construction foreman with severe alcohol use disorder and heavy smoking who joins the practice in 2022 with COPD and steatorrhea; over four years he is diagnosed with chronic pancreatitis, Leriche syndrome, alcoholic cirrhosis, stage IA right upper lobe NSCLC treated with SBRT, and recurrent alcoholic hepatitis with two admissions. Today he is on diuretics for ascites, still drinking and smoking.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

52 y/o construction foreman establishing care. Last saw a doctor several years ago; was told he had COPD by a prior physician around 2016, no records he can name, still fills his inhalers.

CC: belly pain and weight loss.

HPI: About 6 weeks of a gnawing ache high in the abdomen, comes and goes, worse after big meals. Belt is looser, thinks he has lost 'a good chunk' though he doesn't own a scale. Stools are loose, 3 or so a day, greasy and smelly, hard to flush. No blood, no black stools, no vomiting. Appetite is fair. No fever.

Alcohol: drinks every day and has for well over 25 years, mostly beer, lately more liquor. Did not want to put a number on it today. Has never tried to stop and has never had a withdrawal seizure. Wife has been after him about it.
Tobacco: about a pack a day for 30 years, 30 pack-years. Not ready to quit; we talked about it briefly.
No drug use.

PMH: COPD (prior physician, ~2016). Uses albuterol a few times a week, ipratropium most days.
PSH: none.
Meds: albuterol HFA 2 puffs q4-6h prn; ipratropium HFA 2 puffs QID.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father had a drinking problem and cirrhosis, also lung cancer; died of a heart attack at 63. Mother had COPD; died of breast cancer at 70. Brother has coronary disease.
SH: married, lives in Northampton. Foreman for a commercial builder, on his feet all day.

ROS: as above. Mild morning cough, at baseline. No chest pain. No leg swelling.

Exam: Vitals in flowsheet. Weight 90.5 kg, height 178 cm. Alert, smells of tobacco. No jaundice. Lungs with mildly prolonged expiration, no wheeze. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, mild tenderness in the epigastrium, no guarding, no mass, liver and spleen not felt. No edema. Skin without rash.

AUDIT-C 12. PHQ-9 5.

A/P:
1. Upper abdominal pain, weight loss, greasy loose stools in a heavy drinker: concern for pancreatic insufficiency / chronic pancreatitis. CMP, CBC, lipase, GGT, PT/INR today. Referred to GI.
2. Alcohol use disorder, severe. Long talk. He is not ready to commit to stopping. Starting thiamine 100 mg, folic acid 1 mg and a multivitamin daily. Warned not to stop abruptly on his own without calling us.
3. COPD. Continue albuterol and ipratropium; refills sent.
4. Tobacco: advised to quit, open door.
5. Health maintenance: Tdap, PCV20, flu and bivalent COVID today. HCV and HIV screens. Low-dose CT for lung screening ordered. Colon screening: will give a FIT kit at the next visit.

RTC after GI, sooner prn.

documents.title: Your Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Viktor, your blood work is back. Your liver tests are up in the pattern we see with heavy drinking, which is one more reason to cut back. Your lipase (a pancreas enzyme) is normal, but that does not rule out the kind of pancreas problem I am worried about, so the GI visit still matters. Blood counts, kidneys and sugar are fine, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Gastroenterology should call you to schedule. Let me know if you don't hear from them in a week.

documents.body: Spoke with pt about where he used to be seen. He doesn't remember the name of the office that told him he had COPD, thinks it closed. Pharmacy fill history for his inhalers pulled instead and scanned. No outside records to request at this time.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
INDICATION: Chronic upper abdominal pain, weight loss, steatorrhea.
TECHNIQUE: Axial CT of the abdomen and pelvis after IV contrast, with coronal and sagittal reformats.
FINDINGS: Scattered punctate calcifications throughout the pancreas. No pancreatic mass. No peripancreatic fluid collection. Liver without focal lesion. Gallbladder unremarkable; no biliary dilatation. Spleen normal in size. Adrenals and kidneys unremarkable. No ascites. No free air. Bowel nondilated. No adenopathy. Lung bases clear.
reports.conclusion: Scattered pancreatic calcifications, consistent with chronic pancreatitis. No mass or collection.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside Gastroenterology Consultation
Date of service: 12/12/2022
Referred by: Primary Care

Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Pelletier, 52, for upper abdominal pain and weight loss.

He describes about three months of a dull upper abdominal ache with weight loss he did not intend. Bowel movements are loose, three or four a day, foul smelling and difficult to flush. No hematochezia or melena.

He tells me he drinks a bottle of wine a day. He smokes. Medications: albuterol, ipratropium, thiamine, folic acid, multivitamin. NKDA.

Exam: mild tenderness in the epigastrium; no rebound or guarding. No jaundice.

Data: serum lipase normal. Fasting glucose mildly elevated. CT abdomen with contrast (today): scattered calcifications through the pancreas, no mass or fluid collection.

Impression: chronic pancreatitis, almost certainly alcohol related, with exocrine insufficiency (steatorrhea, weight loss). A normal lipase is expected at this stage.

Recommendations:
- Pancrelipase (Creon) 36,000 lipase units with each meal and snack; omeprazole 20 mg daily to help the enzymes work.
- Low-fat diet, smaller meals. Stopping alcohol entirely is the most important step and was discussed at length.
- Follow the fasting glucose in primary care.
- We will see him back as needed.

Thank you for this referral.
Gastroenterology

S: Back after GI. Chronic pancreatitis on CT. Taking Creon with meals, most of the time; stools are down to 1-2 a day and firmer. Omeprazole daily. Upper belly ache is milder.
Still drinking daily. Still smoking.
New: for a couple of months his buttocks, thighs and calves ache and tighten when he walks the job site, has to stop and stand a few minutes, then can go again. Both sides. No pain at rest. No foot sores.

O: Wt 88.0 kg (down from 90.5). Vitals otherwise in flowsheet. Lungs as before. Femoral pulses faint on both sides; pedal pulses hard to feel. Feet cool, no ulcers. Abdomen soft, mildly tender epigastrium.

A/P:
1. Chronic pancreatitis with exocrine insufficiency - better on Creon. Continue. Low-fat diet reviewed.
2. Bilateral buttock/thigh/calf claudication with weak femoral pulses in a heavy smoker - suspect aortoiliac disease. Referred to cardiology (vascular clinic) for evaluation and testing.
3. AUD, tobacco - discussed again. Not ready.
4. Lung screening CT has not been scheduled; radiology left him two messages. He will call them.
5. FIT kit given.

RTC 3 months.

documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology / Vascular Medicine Consultation
Date of service: 03/15/2023
Reason for referral: bilateral claudication

Mr. Pelletier is a 52-year-old foreman referred by his primary care physician. He was seen by gastroenterology in December for chronic pancreatitis. Before joining his current practice last October he had gone several years without seeing any physician.

With roughly 50 meters of walking he gets a tight, aching pain in both calves, both thighs and both buttocks. A few minutes of standing still relieves it. He denies chest pain and dyspnea.

Tobacco: 30 pack-years, still smoking. Alcohol: heavy daily use. Meds: albuterol, ipratropium, thiamine, folic acid, multivitamin, Creon, omeprazole. NKDA.
Family: brother with coronary artery disease; father died of MI.

Exam: BP 138/84, HR 76, BMI 27. Femoral and dorsalis pedis pulses are markedly reduced on both sides. Both legs are cool with loss of hair; no ulceration. There is mild weakness of the lower extremities, ankle reflexes are diminished bilaterally, and pinprick is reduced over both feet. Heart regular without murmur. Lungs clear.

Testing today:
- Ankle-brachial index: 0.64 right, 0.59 left.
- Aortoiliac arterial duplex: occlusion of the distal infrarenal aorta extending into both common iliac arteries, with collateral reconstitution of both external iliac arteries. Monophasic waveforms in both common femoral arteries.

Assessment: aortoiliac occlusive disease (Leriche syndrome) with bilateral claudication.

Plan:
- Start aspirin 81 mg daily and atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
- Daily walking program, walking to the point of moderate pain, resting and repeating.
- Smoking cessation is essential; strongly advised.
- Medical therapy first. Revascularization is not planned at this point; we will reassess if symptoms progress or rest pain or tissue loss develops.
- Lipid panel and LFTs in 6 weeks through primary care.

Thank you for allowing us to participate in his care.
Cardiology

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Cardiology letter reviewed: aortoiliac occlusive disease (Leriche), ABI 0.64 R / 0.59 L, started aspirin 81 and atorvastatin 40, walking program, no revascularization for now.

S: Taking aspirin and atorvastatin, no muscle aches. Tries to walk at lunch, still stops at about the same distance. Creon working; stools mostly formed. Still drinking, still smoking, about a pack a day.

O: Wt 85.0. Vitals in flowsheet. Femoral pulses faint bilaterally. Feet cool, no wounds. Lungs prolonged expiration. Abdomen soft, nontender today.

A/P:
1. Leriche syndrome / aortoiliac disease - continue aspirin, atorvastatin, walking. Lipids and LFTs today as cardiology asked.
2. Smoking is the biggest thing for his legs and lungs. He knows. Declines help right now.
3. AUD - still daily. Encouraged.
4. Chronic pancreatitis - stable on Creon.
5. COPD - stable.

RTC 6 weeks.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your LDL cholesterol dropped nicely on atorvastatin. The liver tests are still elevated, a bit more than in October, which fits with the drinking more than with the statin. Keep taking both new medicines. See you in June.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with his wife, who called to make the appointment.

S: Wife says for the past several months he has been short-tempered and wiped out, napping after work, which he never did. He has had trouble keeping up on the job and has missed some days. He thinks it's the heat and the hours. Says his pants are tighter around the belly even though his face looks thinner. Drinking: wife says it is a fifth of vodka most days now; he did not disagree. No vomiting blood, no black stools.

O: Wt 87.5 (up from 85.0). Vitals in flowsheet. Tired-appearing. Abdomen looks full; hard to examine well today.

A/P:
1. Fatigue, irritability, increasing girth in a heavy drinker - concerned about progression of liver disease. Called GI myself; they will move his follow-up up to early August and do labs there.
2. AUD - wife present; we talked frankly about what the drinking is doing. He agreed to the GI visit.
3. Work note given for missed days.

RTC after GI.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside Gastroenterology Clinic Note
Date of service: 08/09/2023

Mr. Pelletier returns, seen earlier than planned at his PCP's request. Since his GI visit in December and his cardiology evaluation in March, his wife has noticed him changing over about six months: he is more irritable, and he tires so easily that he is struggling to keep his job as a foreman.

Social: current smoker, 30 pack-years. Drinking has climbed over the past 10 years; he now drinks about a fifth of vodka a day.
Meds: albuterol, ipratropium, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, thiamine, folic acid, multivitamin, Creon 36,000 with meals and snacks, omeprazole 20. NKDA.

Exam: Enlarged breast tissue on both sides. Small testes. Thinning of axillary and pubic hair. Numerous spider angiomas across the chest; palmar erythema. The abdomen is distended with a fluid wave, consistent with ascites.

Labs today: albumin 2.9 g/dL, total bilirubin 2.8 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 120 U/L, AST 180 U/L, ALT 150 U/L, PT 16 seconds.

Impression: alcoholic cirrhosis with ascites, decompensated.

Plan:
- Complete abstinence from alcohol. He was told plainly that continued drinking will shorten his life.
- 2 g sodium diet.
- Labs through primary care.
- Return to GI in 6 months or sooner.

Gastroenterology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
GI note from 8/9 reviewed: decompensated alcoholic cirrhosis with ascites; albumin 2.9, bili 2.8, AST 180, ALT 150, PT 16. Plan was abstinence, low sodium, GI in 6 months.

S: He says the GI doctor 'scared him straight.' Has been drinking less this past week, says beer instead of vodka; wife at work today. Belly still big but not tight. No confusion that he notices. No bleeding.

O: Wt 86.8. Vitals in flowsheet. Spider angiomas on chest. Abdomen distended, soft, nontender. No edema. No asterixis.

A/P:
1. Alcoholic cirrhosis with ascites. Repeat CMP, CBC, INR today. Reinforced no alcohol, 2 g sodium diet; low-sodium handout given. Call for fever, belly pain, confusion, black stools or vomiting blood.
2. AUD severe, AUDIT-C 12. Offered referral to addiction treatment; he wants to try on his own first. Warned about withdrawal and to call if shaky or sweaty.
3. Hepatitis B vaccine #1 (Heplisav-B) today given the cirrhosis; #2 in a month.
4. Leriche, pancreatitis, COPD - unchanged.

RTC 3 months; nurse visit next month for vaccines.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for Heplisav-B dose 2 (series complete), flu and updated COVID. Screening questions negative. Heplisav R deltoid, flu L deltoid, COVID L deltoid lower. VIS given. Tolerated. Left for work at 7:50.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Stopped the vodka after the GI visit and is drinking beer only, 'three or four most nights,' wife agrees it is less. Belly has gone down; belt back to the old notch. More energy, back to full days. Still about a pack a day. Taking Creon, omeprazole, aspirin, atorvastatin, vitamins. Legs the same with walking.

O: Wt 86.0. Vitals in flowsheet. Sclerae anicteric today. Abdomen soft, not distended, no fluid wave. A few spider angiomas on chest. No edema.

A/P:
1. Alcoholic cirrhosis - clinically better with less drinking; ascites no longer apparent. Labs today. Keep sodium low.
2. AUD - real progress, AUDIT-C down to 7. Goal is still zero. Praised the change.
3. Tobacco - advised to quit.
4. Shingrix #1 today; #2 at the physical in January.
5. Leriche, COPD, pancreatitis stable.

RTC January for physical.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news, Viktor: your liver numbers are clearly better than in August. Bilirubin and liver enzymes are coming down and the albumin (protein the liver makes) is up. That is what cutting back looks like on paper. Keep going.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

53 y/o M. Interval: cirrhosis diagnosed by GI in August with ascites; since then drinking beer only, a few most nights. Feels better than last summer. Working full time.

Problems: alcoholic cirrhosis (ascites resolved clinically); chronic pancreatitis on Creon; aortoiliac occlusive disease (Leriche) on aspirin/statin; COPD; AUD severe; tobacco.

Meds: albuterol prn, ipratropium QID, Creon 36,000 with meals and snacks, omeprazole 20, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, thiamine 100, folic acid 1, MVI. NKDA.

ROS: morning cough as usual, no change. Claudication at about the same distance. Stools formed. No bleeding, no confusion. Sleeps OK.

Exam: Wt 86.5. Vitals in flowsheet. No icterus. Mouth and neck normal; no lymphadenopathy. Lungs with prolonged expiration, no crackles. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nondistended, no fluid wave. Spider angiomas on chest. Femoral pulses faint. Feet cool, intact skin. No edema. Mood good.

AUDIT-C 7. PHQ-9 4.

A/P:
1. Health maintenance: Shingrix #2 today (series done). FIT kit given. Lung screening CT still never scheduled despite reminders; radiology will call him again and he promised to answer this time. Flu/COVID done in the fall.
2. Cirrhosis: CMP, CBC, INR, GGT today. GI follow-up due next month.
3. Lipids on atorvastatin today.
4. AUD: reduced but not stopped. Goal remains zero.
5. Tobacco: advised, declines.

RTC 3 months.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: FIT negative. Portal message sent. Next due January 2025.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside Pulmonology Consultation
Date of service: 02/20/2024

Reason: persistent cough and weight loss.

Mr. Pelletier is 53, with COPD, ongoing tobacco use, chronic pancreatitis, alcoholic cirrhosis and Leriche syndrome. He reports three weeks of a cough that will not go away, with about ten pounds of weight loss. He has had no fevers, no night sweats and has not coughed up blood.

Family history: lung cancer in his father.
Social: current smoker, about 30 pack-years. Daily alcohol.
Meds: albuterol, ipratropium, aspirin, atorvastatin, Creon, omeprazole, thiamine, folic acid, multivitamin. NKDA.

Exam: afebrile. Respiratory rate 18, SpO2 94% on room air. Diminished breath sounds over the right upper lobe. No clubbing. No lymphadenopathy.

Chest radiograph today: 2 cm nodule in the right upper lobe.

Assessment: right upper lobe nodule in a heavy smoker, concerning for primary lung cancer.

Plan:
- CT chest this week.
- CT-guided biopsy to follow if the CT supports it.
- Oncology referral once tissue is obtained.

Pulmonology

reports.text:
INDICATION: 2 cm right upper lobe nodule on radiograph.
TECHNIQUE: CT of the chest with IV contrast.
FINDINGS: 2.0 cm nodule in the right upper lobe with spiculated margins. No other pulmonary nodules. No hilar or mediastinal lymphadenopathy by size criteria. No pleural effusion. Heart and great vessels normal in caliber. Limited upper abdomen: no adrenal mass.
reports.conclusion: 2.0 cm spiculated right upper lobe nodule, suspicious for primary lung malignancy.

documents.author: interventional radiology
documents.body:
Outside Procedure Note
Date of service: 02/27/2024
Procedure: CT-guided percutaneous biopsy, right upper lobe nodule (FNA and 20-gauge core x3).
Indication: 2 cm spiculated RUL nodule.
Technique: Prone, posterior approach, local lidocaine. Coaxial needle placed into the nodule under CT guidance.
Complications: none. Post-procedure CT without pneumothorax; 2-hour upright chest radiograph without pneumothorax. Discharged home.
Preliminary cytology: suspicious for malignancy. Final pathology to the ordering pulmonologist and PCP.

Infiltrating non-small cell carcinoma.
Immunohistochemistry: TTF-1 positive; p40 negative.
reports.conclusion: Non-small cell carcinoma, favor adenocarcinoma (TTF-1 positive, p40 negative).

documents.title: Pathology Result Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt and wife with the core biopsy result: non-small cell lung cancer, favoring adenocarcinoma. Explained the next steps: a PET scan to see whether it has spread, breathing tests, then a visit with oncology to decide on treatment. Pulmonology has already placed the PET and PFT orders; I placed the oncology referral and asked for the soonest slot. They asked good questions; wife wrote everything down. Office visit set for after the oncology consult.

documents.title: PET-CT, Skull Base to Mid-Thigh
documents.author: radiology
documents.body:
Outside Imaging Report
Exam: FDG PET-CT, skull base to mid-thigh. Date: 03/05/2024
Indication: Staging of biopsy-proven right upper lobe non-small cell carcinoma.
Findings: The 2 cm right upper lobe nodule is FDG avid, SUVmax 6.8. No FDG-avid hilar or mediastinal lymph nodes. No other pulmonary lesions. No abnormal uptake in the adrenals, liver or skeleton. Physiologic activity elsewhere. Pancreatic calcifications on the CT component.
Impression: FDG-avid right upper lobe primary without nodal or distant disease.

reports.text:
Full pulmonary function testing, pre-treatment evaluation.
FEV1 1.92 L (58% predicted). FEV1/FVC 0.57. Diffusing capacity (DLCO) 55% predicted. Acceptable and reproducible efforts.
reports.conclusion: Moderate airflow obstruction with reduced diffusing capacity, consistent with COPD.

documents.title: Thoracic Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Thoracic Oncology Consultation
Date of service: 03/07/2024

Diagnosis: non-small cell lung cancer of the right upper lobe, adenocarcinoma favored (TTF-1+, p40-), clinical stage IA2 (cT1b N0 M0).

History: 53-year-old foreman presenting with three weeks of cough and a 10-lb weight loss. CXR then CT showed a 2.0 cm spiculated RUL nodule. CT-guided biopsy 2/27: cytology suspicious, core confirms NSCLC. PET-CT 3/5: primary SUVmax 6.8, no nodal or distant uptake. PFTs 3/6: FEV1 1.92 L (58%), FEV1/FVC 0.57, DLCO 55%.

Comorbidities: alcoholic cirrhosis with prior ascites, chronic pancreatitis, aortoiliac occlusive disease, COPD. Current smoker (30 pack-years) and daily drinker.

Discussion: Lobectomy would be the standard approach for a fit patient. In his case, cirrhosis with prior decompensation and his lung function make surgery high risk. He was presented at our multidisciplinary thoracic tumor board on 3/7; the consensus recommendation is stereotactic body radiotherapy with curative intent. Referred to radiation oncology. No systemic therapy is indicated for this stage.

We discussed smoking cessation strongly; it matters for treatment outcome. He is thinking about it.

Follow-up: surveillance CT chest every 6 months after treatment, coordinated by radiation oncology.

Thoracic Oncology

events.reason: discuss lung cancer diagnosis and plan

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with wife to go over the lung cancer diagnosis.

Reviewed: RUL adenocarcinoma (favored), stage IA2, PET negative for spread. PFTs FEV1 58%, DLCO 55%. Tumor board recommends SBRT; radiation oncology consult Thursday.

S: Cough a bit better. Scared but 'glad it's small.' Eating OK. Has been drinking a few beers most nights still. Smoking less this week, maybe half a pack.

O: Wt 81.5. Vitals in flowsheet. Lungs unchanged. Biopsy site healed.

PHQ-9 7 - situational; declines counseling referral for now.

A/P:
1. NSCLC RUL, stage IA2 - agree with SBRT plan. Answered questions about radiation; they feel prepared for Thursday.
2. Tobacco - now the best moment to stop; he wants to try cutting down on his own.
3. Cirrhosis, pancreatitis, Leriche, COPD - stable meds.
4. Lung screening order closed; replaced by cancer surveillance with oncology.

RTC 4-6 weeks, after radiation.

documents.title: Radiation Oncology Consultation
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
Radiation Oncology Consultation
Date of service: 03/14/2024

Diagnosis: right upper lobe NSCLC, adenocarcinoma favored, cT1b N0 M0, stage IA2. Medically high risk for resection (cirrhosis, COPD with FEV1 58%).

The nodule is peripheral, away from the central airway. We recommend SBRT, 54 Gy in 3 fractions, every other day. Expected side effects reviewed: fatigue, chest wall soreness, cough, a small risk of radiation pneumonitis or rib fracture. Local control at this size is high.

CT simulation today. Treatment to begin 3/25.

Radiation Oncology

documents.title: Radiation Treatment Summary
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
Radiation Treatment Summary

Site: right upper lobe lung, NSCLC (adenocarcinoma favored), stage IA2.

Outpatient Addiction Psychiatry - Initial Evaluation
Date of service: 08/22/2024
Referral: primary care, for alcohol use disorder in a patient with alcoholic cirrhosis.

He comes in tired, and says he has been feeling bloated a lot lately with some nausea now and then and less of an appetite. He denies abdominal pain, fever or yellowing. He has never had hepatitis and has not traveled.

Substance history: He describes his drinking as 'a few beers most evenings' and frames it as social, part of unwinding with the crew. Tobacco about a pack a day for 30 years. Denies any recreational drug use.

Mental status: cooperative, mildly defensive about drinking, mood 'fine,' affect appropriate, no suicidal ideation, no psychosis, cognition grossly intact.

Exam (limited): liver edge mildly enlarged on palpation. No ascites. I did not see stigmata of chronic liver disease.

Labs drawn before the visit: AST 94, ALT 48, total bilirubin 0.9, alkaline phosphatase 88, albumin 4.2, INR 1.0.

Diagnosis: alcohol use disorder, severe.

Plan:
- Motivational interviewing begun today; he is ambivalent but engaged.
- Referred to outpatient addiction counseling (group and individual).
- Acamprosate offered as a medication compatible with his liver disease; he declined for now.
- Return in 4 weeks.

Addiction Psychiatry

documents.title: Gastroenterology Clinic Note
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside Gastroenterology Clinic Note
Date of service: 02/17/2025

Mr. Pelletier, 54, with alcoholic cirrhosis and chronic pancreatitis, returns. When we last heard from his care team in August he had no jaundice. He now has fatigue, a poor appetite and abdominal discomfort. His wife has noticed his eyes turning yellow and that he is more irritable. He also mentions generalized muscle weakness and nausea at times, without vomiting or diarrhea. No trauma to the abdomen, no travel. He estimates he has lost about 6 kg (13 lb) over the past year without trying.

Family history: father died of a myocardial infarction at 63; mother died of breast cancer at 70.
Social: foreman, and calls the job stressful; says he unwinds with beer after work. Pressed, he acknowledges 8 to 10 beers a day for more than 25 years, plus whiskey on some weekends. A pack of cigarettes daily for 30 years. Eats mostly fast food and packaged snacks; little exercise.
ROS: some trouble sleeping, reduced libido, bruises easily at times. No vomiting of blood, black stools or rectal bleeding. No chest pain, palpitations or dyspnea.

Exam: T 37.0 C, BP 138/84, HR 88, RR 18. Fatigued but alert and oriented. Mild scleral icterus. Palmar erythema. Several spider angiomata over the upper chest and shoulders. Abdomen soft, mildly distended; liver edge firm and mildly tender, 3 cm below the right costal margin. No shifting dullness. Spleen not palpable. No edema.

Labs: AST 178, ALT 74, alkaline phosphatase 250, GGT elevated, total bilirubin 3.1. Albumin mildly low; INR mildly prolonged. Hepatitis B surface antigen and hepatitis C antibody negative.
Ultrasound today: enlarged liver with heterogeneous echotexture, no focal lesion, hepatic vessels patent.

Impression: alcoholic hepatitis on a background of alcoholic cirrhosis.

Plan:
- Percutaneous liver biopsy next week to assess inflammation and fibrosis.
- Complete abstinence; he was told this is now life-threatening.
- High-calorie, high-protein diet; continue Creon.
- Return after biopsy.

Gastroenterology

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: Liver, percutaneous core biopsy.
MICROSCOPIC: Hepatocytes show marked swelling with ballooning degeneration. Lobular inflammation rich in neutrophils. Many hepatocytes contain irregular, rope-like eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions (Mallory-Denk bodies).
reports.conclusion: Ballooning degeneration, neutrophilic inflammation and Mallory-Denk bodies, consistent with alcoholic hepatitis.

Regional Hospital - Internal Medicine Discharge Summary
Admitted: 08/14/2025   Discharged: 08/21/2025

Principal diagnosis: severe alcoholic hepatitis.
Other: alcoholic cirrhosis; chronic pancreatitis; right upper lobe NSCLC s/p SBRT 2024; aortoiliac occlusive disease; COPD; alcohol use disorder, severe; tobacco use.

Presentation: brought in by his wife with weeks of worsening fatigue and jaundice that had become much deeper over the last several days. Biopsy-proven alcoholic hepatitis in February 2025. Continued daily drinking.

Course: Transaminases and bilirubin elevated on arrival. Total bilirubin peaked at 8.4 mg/dL; PT 18.4 seconds (control 12.0), Maddrey discriminant function 38. Infection was excluded before steroids: blood and urine cultures negative. Prednisolone 40 mg daily was started 8/15 for a planned 28-day course. Day-7 Lille score 0.31, consistent with response, so steroids were continued. Monitored for withdrawal; no complications. Nutrition consulted. Abstinence counseling given; he expressed willingness to stop.

Discharge medications: prednisolone 40 mg daily through 9/11/2025 (then stop, no taper); albuterol HFA prn; ipratropium HFA QID; pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals and snacks; omeprazole 20 mg daily; aspirin 81 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily; thiamine 100 mg daily; folic acid 1 mg daily; multivitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with CMP, CBC, INR; gastroenterology in 4 weeks. Complete alcohol abstinence.

Regional Hospital Emergency Department
Date of service: 02/09/2026

Chief complaint: yellow skin, swollen belly, feeling unwell for 2 weeks.

HPI: 55-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis, prior severe alcoholic hepatitis (steroid-treated 8/2025), chronic pancreatitis, treated right upper lobe lung cancer, aortoiliac occlusive disease and COPD. Over two weeks his jaundice has steadily deepened, his abdomen has swelled and he has felt generally unwell. He says he has been drinking a fifth of vodka a day for the past ten years.

Meds: per PCP list (inhalers, Creon, omeprazole, aspirin, atorvastatin, thiamine, folic acid, multivitamin). NKDA.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Scleral icterus. Abdomen distended with a fluid wave, consistent with ascites. Liver palpable 3 cm below the right costal margin; mildly tender in the right upper quadrant. No peripheral edema. Alert and oriented.

Labs: AST 220 IU/L, ALT 90 IU/L, GGT 300 IU/L, total bilirubin 5.2 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 3.1 mg/dL, albumin 2.9 g/dL, PT 18 s (control 12 s), ferritin 900 ng/mL.

MDM: decompensated alcoholic liver disease with new ascites and recurrent alcoholic hepatitis. Needs diagnostic paracentesis to exclude infection and inpatient care.

Disposition: admitted to hospital medicine.

Regional Hospital - Hospital Medicine Discharge Summary
Admitted: 02/09/2026 (via ED)   Discharged: 02/13/2026

Principal diagnosis: alcoholic hepatitis with ascites, on alcoholic cirrhosis.
Other: chronic pancreatitis; RUL NSCLC s/p SBRT 2024; aortoiliac occlusive disease; COPD; alcohol use disorder, severe; tobacco use.

Course:
- Ascites: diagnostic paracentesis 2/10 - SAAG 1.7, ascitic total protein 1.0 g/dL, PMN 80/uL, culture no growth. No spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. Started spironolactone 100 mg and furosemide 40 mg daily; 2 g sodium diet. Weight down with diuresis.

- Alcohol: monitored for withdrawal without complication. Counseled on abstinence; addiction resources provided.

Discharge medications: NEW spironolactone 100 mg daily; NEW furosemide 40 mg daily. Continue albuterol prn, ipratropium QID, pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals and snacks, omeprazole 20 mg, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, thiamine 100 mg, folic acid 1 mg, multivitamin.
